answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A cedar delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A harbor check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A island penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 7799 identities need 7799 bonds of 57 tokens, 37638 dollars of hardware and 35 days of cover.
